lawyer:
Md. Nurul Huq with AKM Shahidul Hoque, Shameem Khaled Ahmed and Tania Siddiqua, Advocates ----- For the Defendant-Petitioners
TH Khan with Miah Abdul Gafur, ABM Abbasuddin and Zahirul lslam Bhuiyan, Advocate ----- For the Plaintiff Opposite-Party Nos 1-9 and 11.
parties:
Chairman, Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka and others ----- Petitioners
Vs.
Motijheel Model High School & others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
2. Facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that the defendant Nos. 1-4 are the petitioners before this court and the opposite party Nos. 1-11 are the plaintiffs in the suit. Plaintiffs instituted the aforesaid suit for declaration that the Order No. 191(Kha)/Dhaka/Da/8163 dated 22.6.92 issued under the signature of the Inspector of Schools of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board, Dhaka, is illegal, inoperative, void and malafide, The case of the plaintiffs, in short, is that Motijheel Model High School held election for formation of the managing Committee of the school on 2.3.92 and in the said election the plaintiff Nos. 2-9 were duly elected from different categories as vice chairman and members of the said Managing Committee. According to Regulation 4 of the Regulations of 1977, namely, the Managing Committee for the Recognised Non-Government Secondary School Regulations as framed under section 39 of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1961, (E.P. Ordinance No. 33 of 1961), the Chairman of the Managing Committee will be the Deputy Commissioner of the district concerned, or Additional Deputy Commissioner or a Magistrate or Upazila Nirbahi Officer nominated by the Deputy Commissioner. The Head Master of the School would be the Member-Secretary of the Managing Committee. After the election was over, the Head Master forwarded the list of the elected vice-president and members to the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, hereinafter referred to the Board, on 3.4.92 in order to form the full-fledged committee. The Deputy Commissioner by his Memo No.153 Shikha/1992 dated 29.3.92 nominated Mr. ASM Mobaidul Islam, Joint  Secretary, Ministry of Flood Control, Government of Bangladesh, to be the Chairman of the committee and forwarded his name to the Chairman of the Board for approval. 

 3. After such nomination a representation from 81 guardians of the students and elites of the area was made to the Ministry of Education bringing several allegations against the plaintiff No. 10 Mr. Mobaidul Islam stating that formerly while he was an Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka, he was the Chairman of the managing committee of the said school in 1986 and during his period as chairman several cases of mismanagement and troubles took place in the school management and he was a partisan with the Head Master, both belonging to the same locality. He disobeyed the orders of the Government while he was the chairman of the managing committee. Further, it was alleged that he was a person who could not be nominated as chairman by the Deputy Commissioner under the relevant Regulations. Ministry of Education forwarded the said representation to the chairman of the Board for taking appropriate action on 19.5.92. The Board after considering the matter found Mr. AKM Abdus Sattar, Joint Chief of Planning Commission of the Ministry of Planning (Defendant No. 7) suitable and recommended him as a fit and impartial person to be nominated as chairman of the managing committee of the said school instead of Mr. Mobaidul Islam. After considering the matter the Ministry approved the said proposal of the Board by its letter dated 16.6.92 and directed the Board to inform all concerned about the decision. Accordingly, the Board by its Memo No. 191 (Kha) Dhaka/Da/8163 dated 22.6.92 approved the entire elected committee with Mr. AKM Abdus Sattar, the Joint Chief of Planning Commission as chairman of the managing committee instead or Mr. Mobaidul Islam. This approval of the full-fledged committee was intimated to all concerned including the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, the Ministry as well as the Head Master cum-Secretary of the school. 

 4. On receipt of the said Memo of the Board dated 22.6.92, the Head Master of the school along with elected vice-chairman and other members and also the person nominated by the Deputy Commissioner, namely, the Joint Secretary Mr. Mobaidul Islam filed this Title Suit No.119 of 1992 in the Third Court of the Subordinate Judge, Dhaka. with a prayer for declaration that the Memo dated 22.6.92. issued by the Board nominating Mr. AKM Abdus Sattar as Chairman of the said managing committee was malafide, motivated, unauthorised, without jurisdiction, illegal, arbitrary and contrary to the regulation and null and void. The plaintiffs also filed an application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a prayer for restraining the defendant Nos. 1-4 and defendant No. 7 from giving effect to the said Memo dated 22.6.92 and not to interfere with the peaceful functions of the plaintiffs as the managing committee of the school. On such application under Order XXXIX, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court issued notices upon defendant Nos. 1-3 and 6 and 7 asking them to show cause within seven days as to why the temporary injunction as prayed for should not be granted. 

 5. In the aforesaid suit plaintiff No. 1 is the school represented by the Head Master-cum-Secretary of the school. Plaintiff No. 2 is the Vice-Chairman of the managing committee of the school. Plaintiff Nos. 3-9 is the elected members of the managing committee from different categories of voters. Plaintiff No. 10 is Mr. ASM Mobaidul Islam who was nominated by the Deputy Commissioner as chairman of the managing committee and plaintiff No. 11 is the Head Master-cum-ex-officio Secretary of Motijheel Model High School. Present petitioner Nos. 1-4 were the defendants and opposite party Nos. 12, 13 and 14 were the proforma-defendants in the suit. 

 9. On this point Mr. Huq has advanced two arguments. One is, that under the aforesaid Regulation 4(1)(a) the Deputy Commissioner was authorised to make himself the Chairman or he may nominate the Additional Deputy Commissioner or a Magistrate or Upazila Nirbahi Officer as the Chairman of the managing committee of such a school. Other one is, that from the proviso it appears that in special cases the Board may, with the approval of the Government, nominate any local distinguished person interested in education as Chairman for any school located anywhere within the jurisdiction of the Board. Mr. Nurul Huq submits that the plaintiff No. 10 Mr. Mobaidul Islam nominated by the Deputy Commissioner as Chairman of the managing committee of the school was neither the Deputy Commissioner nor Additional Deputy Commissioner nor Magistrate nor Upazila Nirbahi Officer. As such, he is a person not authorised by law to be nominated as Chairman of the managing committee for such a school. Mr. Nurul Huq further submits that the impugned order dated 22.6.92 was issued by the Board with the approval of the Government and, as such, the Board acted in pursuance of the proviso to Regulation 4(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the aforesaid Regulations of the Board. Since the Board acted within its jurisdiction, the bar under section 45 of the Ordinance is complete inasmuch as the authority acted with jurisdiction in issuing the order dated 22.6.92. 

 10. He further submits that on another ground the civil suit may not be a bar in spite of the barring provisions if, prima facie, it can be shown from the plaint itself that the order under challenge in the suit was issued malafide by the authority. Mr. Huq has drawn our attention to different paragraphs of the plaint of the suit. He submits that only in paragraph 18 a general allegation was made to the effect that the impugned order of the Board under challenge is illegal, inoperative, malafide, void and arbitrary, and as such, the same may be declared illegal and void. Mr. Nurul Huq submits that no allegation of malafide was disclosed by showing the circumstances of the case. We are to see whether there was any bad motive or illegal motive of the Board of the Government or the person nominated by the Board in the matter of issuing such an order or nomination of Chairman of the managing committee dated 22.6.92. He submits that since Deputy Commissioner nominated a person outside the ambit of Regulation 4 and since 81 persons of the locality made several allegations against the plaintiff No. 10, Mr. Mobaidul Islam who previously acted as Chairman of the managing committee of the aforesaid school in 1986 as Additional District Magistrate of Dhaka and in order to avoid such anomaly and criticism, the Board exercised its jurisdiction under the proviso to Regulation 4(1)(a)(i)(ii) of the aforesaid Regulations. He submits that no allegations or circumstances or instances have been brought against the Board or the Government or Mr. Abdus Sattar in order to show prima facie malafide in issuing the aforesaid order dated 22.6.92. So, the present suit is barred under both the above counts. 

 11. Mr. TH Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties, submits that the barring provision may be there in the law itself, but in spite of such a barring provision a civil Court has got jurisdiction to see as to the legality of the order or action if it is made or taken without jurisdiction or with malafide intention. In support of his contentions Mr. Khan has referred to the cases of Ahsan CSP Vs. Republic of Pakistan, 12 DLR (SC) 9, and Secretary of State Vs. Mask and Co. AIR 1940 (PC), 105. Mr. Nurul Huq does not oppose such a proposition of law which has been settled in the aforesaid illustrious decisions. In elaborating his argument Mr. Khan submits that in the present case the proviso in Regulation 4 is not at all attracted inasmuch as this proviso qualifies only sub-clause (ii) of clause (a) of Regulation 4(1) of the aforesaid Regulations. We are unable to accept the above contentions of Mr. Khan. From reading the Regulation itself it appears to us that this proviso relates to both sub-clauses (i) and (ii) of clause (a) of Regulation 4(1). So, prima facie it appears to us that the person, namely, Mr. Mobaidul Islam nominated by the Deputy Commissioner was not a competent person within this Regulation No. 4 and that the Board treating it as a special case nominated Mr. Abdus Sattar as the Chairman of the managing committee of the said school with the approval of the Government instead of Mr. Mobaidul Islam. So, the question of acting without jurisdiction by the Board does not, prima facie appear in the present case. 

 14. Mr. Khan further submits that if malafide has been alleged in the plaint and in consideration of the assertions made in the plaint if it appears that it is prima facie a case of malafide or an arguable case on the matter of malafide of the authorities concerned, the bar imposed under section 45 of the Ordinance cannot be attracted. It is also a settled principle that if malafide has been alleged and prima facie shown or can be argued, the bar put by barring clause in the law will not be applicable in the suit. The learned Advocate had produced before us a copy of the plaint for consideration. In the impugned order the learned Subordinate Judge found that since there are allegations of malafide against the defendants, the suit in the present nature can be entertained although there is a barring clause under section 45 of the Ordinance. But unfortunately, in a very short-cut manner he has reached a conclusion in this matter without considering the real assertions made in the plaint. Mr. TH Khan submits that in paragraph 18 of the plaint the malafide has been summarised and in the foregoing paragraphs the malafide has been alleged clearly. The plaintiffs in the present suit have challenged the order dated 22.6.92 issued by the Board by which the Board nominated Mr. Abdus Sattar as Chairman instead of Mr. Mobaidul Islam and all other elected members and vice-chairman were kept in tact. Considering the legal position as well as the allegation against Mr. Mobaidul Islam the Board took such an action with the approval of the Government. The plaintiffs ought to have alleged the malafide against the Government or the Board or Mr. Abdus Sattar and the circumstances must be shown to the effect that with bad motive or with bad intention the Board or the Government had nominated Mr. Abdus Satar or with a bad motive to harass Mr. Mobaidul Islam the present order, namely order dated 22.6.92, was passed. Such an allegation or the circumstances showing malafide against the Board or the Government or Mr. Abdus Sattar in connection with the passing of the order dated 22.6.92 are totally absent in the plaint of the suit. Mr. Nurul Huq submits that omnibus allegations of malafide in the plaint is absolutely irrelevant. The malafide must be shown against the Board or the Government or Abdus Sattar in issuing the order dated 22.6.92. Plaintiffs in the present suit have prima facie failed to make out a case of malafide against them. We have perused the plaint as a whole and we are of the view that the plaintiffs have failed to make out a case of malafide in the matter of issuance of order dated 22.6.92. In that view of the matter we do not find any substance in the contentions of Mr. TH Khan. So, the findings of malafide as made by the lower Court in the impugned order have no basis at all. 

 15. Mr. Khan has referred to the case of St. Md. Junaid Vs. Turner Morrison and Co. Ltd. 26 DLR 111. In this judgment it is held by a Division Bench that rejection of a plaint is not identical with dismissal of the suit. Rejection of plaint under rule 11 of Order VII does not preclude a fresh suit under rule 13 CPC. But still rejection of a plaint should not be hastily made without affording opportunity to the plaintiff either to cure the defect or to amend the plaint. The power of rejection of a plaint under rule 11 of Order VII shall be exercised only if, the Court comes to the conclusion on mere reading of the plaint that even if all the allegations are proved the plaintiff would not be entitled to any relief whatsoever. Mr. TH Khan relied upon this decision. Here in this case all the elected members are kept in tact by the impugned order of the Board excepting the Chairman nominated by the Deputy Commissioner. Prima facie it shows that this nomination of Mr. Mobaidul Islam by the Deputy Commissioner does not come within the scope of Regulation No. 4 of the Regulations. Even if everything is admitted, even then this relief sought for by the plaintiffs cannot be given in view of the fact that the relief is sought for such a person who is totally disqualified to become a Chairman of the managing committee of the school in the present case. In that view of the matter, we find that this decision helps the defendant petitioners more than the plaintiffs. Considering the submissions as made by the learned Advocates and also perusing the plaint as a whole, we are of the view that prima facie no case of malafide has been made out against the Board or the Government or Mr. Abdus Sattar in respect of issuance of the order dated 22.6.92 which has been challenged in the suit seeking a decree in declaratory nature. 

 16. Further, it appears that Order VII, rule 11 clause (a) of the Code of Civil Procedure speaks that a plaint can be rejected if the cause of action is not disclosed, Mr. TH Khan submits that cause of action may be one or may be several. But the cause of action should be gathered from the reading of the plaint as a whole. There are as many as 11 plaintiffs. Mr. Khan submits that they have jointly filed the suit challenging the order of the Board dated 22.6.92. Excepting plaintiff No. 10, namely, Mr. Mobaidul Islam, all other plaintiffs, on the face of it, have no grievance or any cause of action against the impugned order dated 22.6.92 inasmuch as their interests have not been at all affected and they are not aggrieved or prejudiced in any manner whatsoever. Only the case of plaintiff No. 10 Mr. Mobaidul Islam can be said that be may be in some manner affected; that on the face of it he is not an authorised person to be nominated as chairman as contemplated under Regulation 4 of the Regulations and, as such, prima facie he has no cause of action at all in the present suit in view of the fact that any sort of legal right or statutory character of this plaintiff No. 10 has been created and subsequently affected by the impugned order. The cause of action as disclosed in the plaint, in our view, cannot be called as a cause of action for challenging the present order dated 22.6.92 in view of the fact that out of 11 plaintiffs. 10 plaintiffs have no grievance at all and the remaining person, namely plaintiff No. 10, has no legal right in order to claim the office of the chairman of the managing committee of the said school. In that view of the matter, we hold that regarding cause of action the plaintiffs have totally failed to make out any case in the plaint itself. 

 17. Mr. Nurul Huq submits that the life of the managing committee is for three years and already about one and half years have passed under this litigation. It is an educational institution and if the litigation likes this is going on in between the school committee and the controlling authority, the Government and supervising authority, the Board, it will be detrimental to the interest of the school itself. He further submits that it is absolutely a frivolous and vexatious litigation inasmuch as neither any interest nor any legal right of any of the plaintiffs has been affected by the issuance of the order dated 22.6.92. We find that all the plaintiffs will not gain any benefit out of this suit. Out of 11 plaintiffs, 10 plaintiffs had no interest in this suit and we fail to understand what interest led them to challenge the present order in the court of law without having any personal benefit. It seems, it is the desire of the plaintiffs that the Board or the Government should nominate a person as Chairman according to their desire and the Board cannot independently take any action in the matter of nominating the Chairman of the managing committee. Such a desire is absolutely frivolous. Deputy Commissioner nominated Mr. Mobaidul Islam as Chairman while Board nominated Mr. Abdus Sattar instead of Mobaidul Islam. It may be a dispute at best between the Deputy Commissioner and the Board, but the plaintiffs have no grievance in such a matter. Since no useful purpose will be served in such a litigation. Mr Huq submits, such a vexatious suit should not be allowed to continue by the court of law and if it is allowed, it will cause detriment, injury and prejudice to the interest of the school. 

 "Any person entitled to any legal character, or to any right as to any property, may institute a suit against any person denying, or is interested to deny, his title to such character or right, and the court may in its discretion make therein a declaration that he is so entitled, and the plaintiff need not in such suit ask for any further relief: 

 Provided that no court shall make any such declaration where the plaintiff, being able to seek further relief than a mere declaration, omits to do so" 

 20. From mere reading of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act it appears to us that the present suit is hit by that section on its very face inasmuch as the plaintiffs are not entitled to either any legal character or any legal right as to any property or right in challenging the order dated 22.6.92. In the aforesaid decision their Lordships further held as follows: 

 21. Considering the above decision it appears to us that it has got full application in the facts and circumstances of the present case. The preponderant circumstances surrounding this case has led us to arrive at an irresistible conclusion that the court of law should reject the plaint of such a suit under its inherent power even if it is not covered under rule 11(d) of Order 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure and we are doing so. Further, prima facie it is hit by section 42 of the Specific Relief Act inasmuch as the issuance of order dated 22.6.92 has not affected the plaintiffs as to their any legal character or legal right in any of their property or right. In our view, this is absolutely a frivolous suit without having any cause of action or without any grievance of any of the plaintiffs as to any legal character or legal right and only some unknown interest led the members of the managing committee to file such a suit to cause some disadvantages or injury or prejudice to the interest of the school. In this view of the matter, we hold that such a suit should not be allowed to proceed and, as such, the plaint should be rejected. 

 23. Mr. Nurul Huq submits that there are allegations to the effect that the plaintiff No. 11 i.e. Head Master-cum-Secretary and plaintiff No. 10 the said Mr. Mobaidul Islam hail from the same locality and there might be some unknown interest in between them while the latter was the Chairman of the managing committee in 1986 being Additional District Magistrate, Dhaka. Mr. Huq submits, it is difficult to understand as to what led this Head Master-cum-Secretary of the school to institute the present suit against the supervising authority, the Board and the controlling authority, the Government. Mr. Huq further submits, by instituting such a frivolous and vexatious suit, the Head Master-cum-Secretary of the school is squandering away the fund of the school which he is not authorised to do. We find force in the above submissions of Mr. Huq. It is expected that the Head Master-cum-Secretary of the school shall be a neutral person and he shall never quarrel with the supervising authority and the controlling authority for the interest of the school. We desire that the plaintiffs should not be allowed to spend money from the school fund for such fanciful and frivolous litigation. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the arguments and the submissions advanced by the learned advocates and also the legal provisions as discussed above, we are of the view that the learned Subordinate Judge committed an error of law in his decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned order. This application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure will succeed and the plaint is liable to be rejected. 

 In the result, this Rule is made absolute without cost, the impugned order dated 18.11.92 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is hereby set aside, the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure filed by the defendant-petitioners is hereby allowed and the plaint of the aforesaid Title Suit No. 119 of 1992 pending in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, is hereby rejected and the order of status quo in the form of injunction passed by the learned Subordinate Judge is hereby set aside. We direct that all the expenses incurred by the plaintiffs including lawyers fees for the above suit as well as for this Revision Case shall be borne by the plaintiff Nos. 2 to 11 from their own pockets and the same shall not be borne from the fund of the school.
